slot.brief: A current-carrying coil of given turns, area and current: compute its magnetic moment, and possibly the torque in a given field.

stem: A coil of $40$ turns has an area of $5\ \text{cm}^2$ and carries a current of $2$ A. Its magnetic moment is

verdicts.working: Magnetic moment: μ = NIA = 40 × 2 × (5 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 0.04 A·m².

working:
$\mu=NIA$; $A=5\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2$.
$\mu=40(2)(5\times10^{-4})=0.04\ \text{A m}^2$

Independent check: Magnetic moment: μ = NIA = 40 × 2 × (5 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 0.04 A·m².
solution:
Magnetic moment of a coil is $\mu=NIA$; the area is $5\times10^{-4}\,\text{m}^2$.
$$\mu=40\times2\times5\times10^{-4}=0.04\,\text{A m}^2$$
